named_confounds: genre composition shift (early period has far fewer works, juvenile/adventure dominate late)
date uncertainty (low/medium date_confidence for over half of works)
single sampled passage per work (high sampling noise)
sparse early sample (752 pre-1876 works, some genre cells n<60)
rationale: Each work has 1 passage, so the work rate is the DISTANCE_TRAVEL count divided by n_passages (0 or 1). I took the mean rate per genre for early (<1876, n=752) and late (>=1876, n=6014) works, then averaged the late-minus-early differences with equal weight per genre (8 genres). Effect = +0.052. The 95% CI from 1000 bootstrap resamples of works within each genre-period cell is [0.032, 0.069]. Every genre's difference is positive (+0.04 to +0.06). Robustness checks: high-date-confidence works only, +0.049; excluding other/collection, +0.053; within UK +0.039, US +0.032, unknown origin +0.064. Decade means rise fairly steadily, from about 0.04-0.07 before 1880 to about 0.12 after 1890. Caveats: the early cells are small (two genres have 0 hits early); the bootstrap does not cluster by author; only one passage per work was sampled; labels may come from a classifier whose behavior could drift across the period; and corpus selection may favor travel-heavy late genres, though the within-genre weighting reduces that. The cited passages are late-period passages labeled DISTANCE_TRAVEL. They only illustrate the label and do not by themselves show a trend.
